newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT-Thai finance firms profit seen down.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Thai finance firms profit seen down.

text.p: Earnings of eight major Thai finance and securities firms covered by Thaimex Finance and Securities Plc are set to fall by about 80 percent this year, the company said in a report.
"We have forecast the full year 1997 net profit to decline by 79.57 percent year on year," said the report, obtained by Reuters on Friday.

Thaimex covers CMIC Finance and Securities Plc, Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc, General Finance and Securities Plc, Krungthai Thanakit Plc. Nava Finance and Securities Plc, National Finance and Securities Plc, Tisco Plc and Phatra Thanakit Plc.

"Finance and securities revenues are being squeezed on both sides of the market, the economy -- as it refuses to pull out of its nosedive, and also the Bank of Thailand -- through stricter provisioning requirements," the report said.
The central bank has asked finance firms to increase provisioning for low quality assets.
Securities trading revenues fell by 40.3 percent in the first quarter year on year, the company said.
It said it expects brokerage income to decline by 7.17 percent this year against 1996.
The decline in the market will see firms carrying substantial portfolio losses, the report said.

"Although we expect the SET to rise 7.6 percent by year end the increase will not be sufficient to reverse losses during the first half. As a result the total change for the year will be negative 56.7 percent," Thaimex said.

Operating expenses of the eight finance firms declined by 5.9 percent in the first quarter of 1997 against the same period a year earlier but opportunities for further cuts are limited, the report said.

"Unfortunately we do not see that these savings can be repeated in 1997, thus pushing the sector average up slightly by 3.9 percent year on year unless more branches are closed and there are more layoffs," the report said. ($1 = 26 baht)
